full_judgment:
7. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the respondent No. 1 submitted that the original plaintiffs interest and the interest of the defendant No. 6 at the time of filing the suit was contradictory for which she was made a defendant in the suit, so the right to sue did not survive/continue after the death of the original plaintiff as all his heirs, the defendants have contradictory interest in the suit with that of the original plaintiff; that at the time of filing the suit defendant No.  6 was the beneficiary of the gift deed in question but when she is transposed from the category of the defendant to the category of the plaintiff; her interest became antagonistic or contradictory to the interest she had previously as defendants. So, she cannot be transposed from the category of defendant to the category of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that if the plaintiff would have been alive and the suit would be decreed this defendant- appellant would get nothing and if the suit would be dismissed then she as defendant would get a share as donee but if after transposition the suit is decreed she would get 2 anns share of her husband as heir and not as donee. So, her interest in two defendant positions is contradictory and she cannot be transposed as prayed for. The learned Advocate-on-Record finally submitted that out of two deeds being No. 8409 and 8410 under challenge in the suit, the defendant-appellants name appear in one deed No. 8409. So, in another deed No.  8410 she is not a party and as such, she cannot be transposed as sole plaintiff from the category of the defendant in the suit after the death of the original sole plaintiff and the High Court Division is quite justified in making the Rule absolute. 

 "In a suit where deceased plaintiff prayed for declaration that he is real owner of the suit property covered by the deeds of gift and that the defendant No. 6 having no liable interest was entitled to he transposed as plaintiff in order to have the deeds cancelled by way of decree in the suit."
